journal.title: Journal
journal.intro: Notes from the colour room and the floor.

items.title: Balayage or highlights?
items.description: How balayage and foil highlights differ, how they grow out, and which suits how often you want to come in.

photo.alt: Two heads of wavy hair from behind, bright blonde and honey

body: Both lighten parts of your hair. The difference is how the colour goes on, and so how it grows out.
Painted by hand on the surface of the hair, heavier at the ends. There is no line as it grows, so most of our balayage clients come back every three or four months.
Woven into foils from the root. Brighter and more even, and the regrowth shows as a line, so they want a visit every eight to ten weeks.
If you want to come in less, balayage. If you want blonde right up to the root, highlights. Your colourist will say which suits your hair at the consultation.

items.title: Caring for colour
items.description: Five habits that keep colour from fading between visits, and why the skin test matters every time.

photo.alt: Colour brushes standing in a steel pot

body: Colour fades a little with every wash and every hot tool. Five habits slow it down.
Wash in cool water, two or three times a week. Use a colour-safe shampoo. Protect from heat before every blow-dry. A gloss between colours brings the shine back.
Hair dye can cause allergic reactions, even to a colour you have used before. That is why we ask for a skin test at least 48 hours before colour, and again if it has been six months.

items.title: Growing out a cut
items.description: How to grow out a bob or a fringe without an awkward stage: trims every eight weeks, and what to ask for.

photo.alt: Long dark layers, held at the ends

body: Growing out takes patience and small trims. Without them, the shape goes before the length arrives.
Ask for the shape to be kept, not the length taken. A centimetre off the back lets the front catch up.
Sweep it to the side from the start. When it reaches the cheekbone, it can be layered into the rest.

items.text: I tapped my length and the price was there. That was what I wanted to know.

items.text: The colour year went into my calendar and I haven't missed a root since.

questions.q: How do I know what it will cost?
questions.a: Choose your length and the stylist's level at the top of the home page: that's the price. Very thick hair can take longer, and we say before we start.

questions.q: Why does the price change with the stylist?
questions.a: Each stylist works at one of three levels: stylist, senior or director. The price follows the level, so two seniors cost the same.
For colour appointments of two hours or more, £30, taken off the bill. Give us 48 hours' notice to move or cancel and it's returned.
Up to fifteen minutes, we'll still do everything we can. Later than that, we may need to shorten or move the appointment.

questions.q: Do I need a skin test?
questions.a: Yes, if you're new to colour with us or it's been six months. Walk in any time we're open, at least 48 hours before; it takes five minutes.

questions.q: Do I need a consultation first?
questions.a: For a big change, yes. It's fifteen minutes and free. Start it on WhatsApp from the colour consultation page.

questions.q: Can I have colour while pregnant?
questions.a: Ask your midwife or GP first, and talk to your colourist. The NHS has guidance on hair dye in pregnancy.
From two and a half hours for short hair to four for long. The price by length shows the time for yours.
Tell us within seven days and we'll put it right, free.
Yes. There's coffee and a seat by the window.
